author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory
summary: A read-only page listing every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown by full name. One page, no paging, reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: the specialty directory is served at GET /specialties.html
the page lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name
under each specialty, every veterinarian holding it is shown by first name followed by last name (for example "Helen Leary")
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
every specialty renders on one page: no paging control and no page parameter
a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, shown as held by none
with no specialties stored, the page opens and shows an empty directory rather than failing
specialties are presented in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians within each specialty
two stored specialties sharing one name are listed as two entries, not merged
no navigation entry and no link on any other page points at the specialty directory; the page itself carries the standard site navigation, as REQ-SYS-001 requires of every page
inherited from REQ-LANG-002: the page's user-facing wording is not hard-coded and is present in every supported language bundle
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application: NG-2 is unchanged and still covers it
a navigation entry, menu item, or inbound link from any other page: deliberate product decision for this round, a visible entry point is a possible follow-up request
searching or filtering the specialty directory: NG-9 stands
a machine-readable representation of the specialty listing: REQ-VET-002 was withdrawn and gains no successor here
paging: unlike the veterinarian directory, this page is unpaged by product decision
notes: Open questions recorded rather than waited on, per the product owner's standing instruction; narrowest reading taken in each case. (1) Ordering of specialties and of holders within a specialty is unstated: taken as a stable order, mirroring edge case 1 of the veterinarian directory. (2) Two stored specialties sharing one name: taken as two entries, since nothing in the stored data forbids the duplicate (specialties.name carries a plain index, not a unique constraint). Both are logged in docs/prd.md Open Questions. The last acceptance criterion is inherited from the existing REQ-LANG-002, not new scope: it binds all user-facing wording, and this project ships eleven message bundles. No new domain vocabulary resolved; Veterinarian and Specialty already carry their definitions in docs/ubiquitous-language.md, so that file is unchanged.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the existing server-rendered page pattern applied to a second read surface in the vet feature package: a controller in org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet, Spring Data repository interfaces, a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets/ wrapped in the shared layout fragment, and message-bundle keys. It needs no new module, no new integration, and no departure from the feature-package ADR or the Thymeleaf rendering ADR. The one adjustment is a thin read model: the page groups veterinarians under specialties, which no existing type expresses, so the slice adds a value-object read model plus a pure assembler that builds it from the two repository results. Ordering is the second adjustment and the only load-bearing one, now recorded in docs/system-design.md (Persistence) and its ADR: an unpaged listing computes its order in Java rather than by ORDER BY, so the sequence is identical across H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL instead of following each vendor's collation.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is a new route in the vet feature package; no existing route changes
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data repository over the existing specialties table; it mirrors PetTypeRepository, which is the precedent for a repository over a lookup entity
VetRepository gains one query method returning veterinarians with their specialties join-fetched; the existing findAll() and findAll(Pageable) are untouched

the page joins the site navigation by reusing fragments/layout with a menu key that matches no menuItem, so the standard navigation renders and no entry is added; layout.html is not edited, which is what satisfies the no-inbound-link criterion

new message keys must be added to messages.properties and to every translated bundle under src/main/resources/messages/; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on a key missing from any bundle and on any HTML literal text without a #{} lookup (messages_en.properties is exempt from the key check by fallback convention)
reuse the existing keys vets, specialties, name, and none where the wording already fits, so the translation surface stays as small as the page allows

patterns.description: repository over a lookup entity returning it in a fixed order — the precedent SpecialtyRepository follows
controller shape for a read-only page: bind request, call repository, populate model, return a templates/<feature>/<view> name
rendering a collection with an empty case falling back to the #{none} key — reuse for a specialty held by no veterinarian

Web controller row: the controller binds and delegates and holds no rule. Put the specialties-to-holders grouping in a static factory on the read model, not in the controller — a pure function over the two repository results, unit-testable without the web layer. The brief states plainly that a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing deviation

Value object row: the read model is an immutable record of a Specialty and its ordered holders, one instance per stored specialty. Grouping keys on the specialty identifier, never on its name — that is exactly what makes two specialties sharing one name two entries

risks.risk: a no-argument query method on VetRepository annotated @Cacheable("vets") collides with the existing findAll(): both key on SimpleKey.EMPTY in the same cache, so one method can silently serve the other's result. Both return Collection<Vet>, so the collision type-checks and fails only in behavior — the join-fetch variant excludes veterinarians holding no specialty, so a hit from the wrong entry would put those veterinarians back on the page or drop specialty holders from the vet list
risks.mitigation: leave the new query method uncached. The page is read-only and small, and the vet cache has no eviction configured (Open Questions from the Survey, item 5), so widening its use is the wrong direction. If caching is later wanted, give the method its own cache name rather than sharing "vets"

risks.risk: loading veterinarians without a join fetch triggers one collection query per veterinarian: the ManyToMany is EAGER, so a plain findAll() satisfies it row by row
risks.mitigation: the new query join-fetches the specialties in a single statement, giving the page two queries total — one for all specialties, one for the veterinarians that hold any. Do not build the page by iterating specialties and querying holders per specialty

risks.risk: an inner join fetch drops veterinarians holding no specialty, which is correct for this page but silently wrong if the method is reused for the veterinarian directory
risks.mitigation: name the method for the restriction it carries rather than as a general findAll variant, and leave VetController on its existing methods

risks.risk: ordering by name in SQL would be stable per deployment but different across vendors, repeating the class of divergence already recorded as the PostgreSQL case-sensitive owner search under Known Defects, and invisible to the H2-backed suite
risks.mitigation: order in Java per the new ADR, with the identifier as the final tiebreak so equal names still yield a total order

risks.risk: the empty-directory criterion and the held-by-none criterion are different cases and are easy to conflate: no specialties stored means no entries at all; a specialty with no holders is an entry rendering the #{none} fallback
risks.mitigation: the read model distinguishes them by construction — an empty entry list versus an entry with an empty holder list; assert both separately

notes: Verdict is minor rather than covered because the read model and its assembler are a type shape the codebase does not yet contain, and rather than new because nothing here is a new module, integration, or hard-to-reverse choice. Durable-memory writes: docs/adr/2026-08-28-in-memory-ordering-for-unpaged-listings.md (new, indexed in docs/adr/README.md) and one rule line under docs/system-design.md Persistence carrying the back-link. Nothing else was crystallized; the route, template, and bundle work is routine detail. Contracts-table rows for the new types are deliberately not pre-written, since that table records current state and the code does not exist yet. The two open questions the PRD logged are answered here at design level, both at the narrowest reading: ordering is specialties by name then id, holders by last name then first name then id, computed in Java; two specialties sharing one name stay two entries because grouping keys on the identifier. Residual open question, recorded not escalated: Java String ordering is code-point order, so the sequence is deterministic on every vendor but not locale-collated for readers of the non-Latin bundles — a locale-aware collation was considered out of the narrowest reading and is not implemented. Naming: SpecialtyDirectoryEntry is a proposal, not a constraint; any name from the PRD's own phrasing works, and "holders" for the veterinarian list matches docs/ubiquitous-language.md, which defines a Specialty as held by zero or more Veterinarians. On tests: the assembler is a pure function over real Vet and Specialty instances, which is the real-implementation seam docs/testing-principles.md asks new code to find; reach for MockMvc only for the route, status, view name, and rendered content, and prefer a hand-written repository double over a framework stub for the controller test. No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit. Read basis for the covering-pattern claims is grep and direct file reads, not the IDE symbol oracle, which is not connected in this run.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The threat-model row still reads "one parameterized JPQL query" as the mitigation inventory. This change adds a second @Query (VetRepository.findAllHoldingASpecialty), so the count is now stale: production holds two literal JPQL queries (VetRepository:73 and owner/PetTypeRepository:36), and neither takes a bind parameter at all. The security property the row asserts is unchanged and still true (no string-concatenated SQL, no user input reaching a query string) -- only the count and the word "parameterized" drift. Swept all of src/main/java for @Query: these two are the complete set, so this is the only instance of the class.
findings.fix: Update the mitigation cell to: "Data access is exclusively through Spring Data JPA derived queries and two static JPQL queries, neither of which takes user input; no string-concatenated SQL exists in production code."

approved_aspects: JPQL construction is safe: findAllHoldingASpecialty (VetRepository:73) is a compile-time string constant in the @Query annotation with no parameters, no concatenation, no SpEL, and no Sort/Pageable argument that could inject an order-by fragment. No injection sink exists.

No untrusted input enters the slice: showSpecialtyDirectory (SpecialtyController:40) binds no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestBody, or form object, and declares no @InitBinder surface. The only argument is the framework-supplied Model, so there is no mass-assignment or identifier-tampering vector and no need for the id-disallow binder pattern the other controllers carry.

Read-only end to end: SpecialtyRepository exposes findAll only (deliberately narrow), both repository methods are @Transactional(readOnly = true), and SpecialtyDirectoryEntry is an immutable record whose compact constructor defensively copies holders via List.copyOf. No write path is reachable from the new route, so the unauthenticated-modification threat-model row is not widened.

Output escaping is correct in templates/vets/specialtyList.html: stored specialty names (line 19) and veterinarian first/last names (line 22) render through th:text, which HTML-escapes by default. There is no th:utext, no th:inline='javascript', no attribute-context or URL-context interpolation of stored data, and no th:href preprocessing (__${...}__) on user-derived values anywhere in the new template. Swept all of src/main/resources/templates for th:utext and th:inline: zero hits repository-wide, so stored-XSS via this page is not reachable. The literal 'specialtyDirectory' passed to the layout fragment is a static menu-name argument compared for equality, not rendered as markup.

No new data exposure relative to the existing directory: /vets.html already renders every vet's first and last name with their specialty names to unauthenticated callers, and /vets serializes the same graph as JSON. The new page presents the identical fields under an inverted grouping. The only increment is specialty rows held by no veterinarian -- clinic reference data, not PII, and not a new data class. Judged on its merits rather than on the absent nav link, the exposure of this route equals that of /vets.html, so reachability by URL alone adds no attack surface the existing pages do not already carry.

No secrets in the diff: swept the new Java sources, the template, and the touched docs for token/password/secret/key/credential/apikey. The only hit is docs/prd.md:18, pre-existing prose that cross-references the committed development credentials already recorded in system-design.md#security-context. Nothing new is introduced.

Supply chain is a null delta: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are untouched by the change set (git diff --stat empty), so no new or upgraded dependency enters the tree and no CVE surface changes. The project configures no dependencyCheck plugin, so dependencyCheckAnalyze was not available to run; version-pinned Spring Boot 4.1.0 is unchanged by this slice.

Deliberate cache-poisoning avoidance is correct and worth keeping: the Javadoc at VetRepository:66 explains that findAllHoldingASpecialty is not @Cacheable('vets') because, taking no argument, it would collide with findAll() on SimpleKey.EMPTY and the two could serve each other's results. That collision would have been a real integrity defect (the restricted inner-join result silently answering the unrestricted vet listing, or vice versa); the omission prevents it.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The holder comparator is a three-level tiebreak (last name, then first name, then id), mirroring the specialty comparator's two-level tiebreak (name, then id). The specialty side has a dedicated test pinning its id tiebreak (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListTwoSpecialtiesSharingOneNameSeparately, ids 2 and 9 both named "surgery"), but no test exercises the holder side's final id tiebreak: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldPresentHoldersInAStableOrder only pins the last-name-tie -> first-name-tiebreak level (Ada Douglas before Linda Douglas). Two holders with the same last name AND first name (a realistic clinic scenario, e.g. two vets literally named "Linda Douglas") would exercise Vet::getId as the deciding comparator level, and nothing today would catch a regression there. This is the same ordering-stability property the ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-28-in-memory-ordering-for-unpaged-listings.md) calls out for specialties, left half-pinned for holders.
findings.fix: Add a test (e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldBreakATieOnMatchingHolderNamesByIdentifier) with two Vet instances sharing both first and last name but distinct ids, asserting the lower id sorts first, mirroring theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListTwoSpecialtiesSharingOneNameSeparately's shape.

findings.description: This test walks the filesystem and greps template text; it never touches MockMvc, the injected stub repositories, or any Spring-managed bean. Per testing-principles.md's pyramid guidance ("could this have been tested without booting the framework? If yes, it belongs in a unit and the test belongs in the base of the pyramid"), this is pure JVM logic riding inside a @WebMvcTest class for no structural reason — it could run as a plain JUnit test with zero Spring context, which would also decouple it from ever being skipped by @DisabledInNativeImage/@DisabledInAotMode on the class.
findings.fix: Move this test (and its mentionsTheSpecialtyDirectoryAddress helper) to a plain, non-Spring JUnit test class alongside or in SpecialtyDirectoryEntryTests's package, so it counts toward the unit tier rather than riding on the web-layer test's context.

The vet-holding-no-specialty exclusion (the inner JOIN FETCH restriction) is correctly pinned at the only layer that can observe it: SpecialtyDirectoryRepositoryTests (@DataJpaTest) verifies holder count against a real H2 database seeded from the project's actual data.sql fixture, not an invented one

Two stored specialties sharing one name are proven to stay two entries and to order by identifier (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListTwoSpecialtiesSharingOneNameSeparately), at both the pure-unit and, indirectly through the same grouping-by-id code path, the rendering level

Full-name ("first last") rendering is asserted at the actual rendered HTML via MockMvc content, not just at the read-model level, so a template regression concatenating the fields wrong would be caught

The no-inbound-link acceptance criterion is verified by scanning every real template under src/main/resources/templates for the literal route string, which is a materially stronger check than asserting against a hand-picked list of pages

No mock framework used anywhere in the new tests; StubSpecialtyRepository/StubVetRepository are hand-written real implementations per the brief's mocking policy, and SpecialtyDirectoryRepositoryTests exercises the real Spring Data query against a real database
All 4 prd.md edge cases for REQ-VET-003 and all 9 named test_names in the prd-entry are present and use the project's the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school

Test data construction goes through specialty()/vet() factory methods rather than raw constructors, and named constants (RADIOLOGY, JAMES_CARTER, etc.) carry role-describing names per the three-tier convention; no mystery literals found

i18n wording test (theSpecialtyDirectoryWordingShouldComeFromTheMessageBundles) checks a non-default bundle's actual localized strings rather than the default, catching a hard-coded-string regression that a default-locale-only test would miss
